 Order

Petitioners-accused Nos.1,2,3,8 and 9 who are sought to be prosecuted for the offence punishable under Section 498A, 114, 323, 504,506 r/w 34 of IPC and Section 3 & 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, are before this Court.

Abusaleha vs State Of Karnataka By on 14 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32287346/
2 2.

The case of the prosecution is that, accused No.1 who is the husband, accused Nos.2 and 3 are the parents-in- laws, accused Nos.8 and 9 are the relatives and they subjected the defacto-complainant to cruelty, both mentally and NC: 2023:KHC:28804 physically, and also a demand was made to bring money from her parental home.
3.

Defecto complainant had filed a suit in O.S.No.38/2021 before the Family Court, Davanagere for dissolving her marriage with the accused No.1 and in the said proceedings, parties have amicably settled the disputes and as per the terms of the settlement, the marriage of the defacto- complainant with the accused No.1 has been dissolved mutually and defacto complainant has no objection for quashing the impugned proceedings.
4. Parties are present before this Court with their respective counsels.

5. Though the offences alleged are cognizable and non-compoundable however, having regard to the fact that dispute between the parties having been amicably settled, and the marriage of the accused No.1 and the defacto-complainant having been dissolved mutually, and that the defacto- complainant-respondent No.2 having no objection for quashing the impugned proceedings, it would be a futile exercise, if the petitioners are subjected to trial, since the probability of conviction is remote and bleak.
Hence, the continuation of the criminal proceedings will be an abuse of process of law.
, insofar it relates to petitioners-accused Nos.1,2,3, 8 & 9 is hereby quashed.
